results.summary: This project implements a 4-bit unsigned multiplier using an array multiplier architecture in Verilog. It takes two 4-bit inputs and produces an 8-bit product through partial product generation, shifting, and summation. The design is purely combinational and fits in a 1x1 tile. It was tested with a testbench covering various input pairs, and no external hardware is required.

This project implements an 8-bit carry-lookahead adder in Verilog, designed for fast addition by computing carry bits in parallel using propagate and generate signals. It takes two 8-bit inputs and produces an 8-bit sum, ignoring carry out. The design is fully combinational and was exhaustively tested with all 25536 possible input pairs. No external hardware is needed.

This project is a 4-bit unsigned multiplier implemented in Verilog, accepting two 4-bit inputs and producing an 8-bit product. It uses an array multiplier architecture with partial products and summation. The design is combinational and fits in a 1x1 tile. Testing involves applying several input pairs and checking the output against expected products.

This project implements an 8-bit carry-select adder in Verilog, using two ripple carry adders with different carry inputs and a multiplexer to select the correct sum. It takes two 8-bit inputs and produces an 8-bit sum, ignoring carry out. The design was tested with all possible input combinations. No external hardware is required.

This project is a digital readout for a two-channel time-frequency spectrogram extractor, part of a MEMS-based acoustic emission sensor interface. It processes 7-bit thermometer-coded inputs per channel, decodes them to 3-bit BCD, and performs event-based sampling at 1 MHz for 200 us, storing data in a double buffer for serial readout. The design includes an RTC for timestamping and a state machine for control. It is an early work-in-progress test implementation and requires external analog front-end and a logic analyzer for debugging.

This project is a 15-channel pulse counter designed for acoustic emission detection, counting short digital pulses on each channel and periodically outputting the counts serially. It includes a real-time clock (RTC) for time-stamping, overflow detection, and a readout state machine. The design is an early work-in-progress test implementation and is the second Tiny Tapeout submission, improving on a previous 4-channel version. External hardware such as a logic analyzer is recommended for debugging.

This project is a maze explorer game implemented in Verilog, where the player navigates a maze using three input buttons to move forward and select direction. The game state and direction are output on bidirectional pins, and the maze walls are displayed on five 7-segment displays. It requires external hardware: five 7-segment displays, current-limiting resistors, and wiring. The design is a simple interactive game suitable for educational purposes.

This project implements I2C and SPI communication protocols in Verilog. It provides pins for I2C data and clock, SPI MISO, MOSI, and SCK, along with output enables. The documentation is minimal, stating only that it is a design of I2C and SPI protocols and that testing involves sending data with an enable clock. No external hardware is required, but the lack of detailed documentation limits understanding of the implementation.

This project implements a frequency sweeper in Verilog that generates an output clock whose frequency is divided by 2 every 15 clock cycles, cycling from 1/2 to 1/16 of the input clock frequency. It has an active-high enable input and a single clock output. The design includes a testbench and Python script for simulation, and for hardware testing, an oscilloscope is needed to observe the output. It is a simple clock generation experiment.

This project is a simple RISC-V processor design in Verilog that fetches, decodes, and executes instructions using an ALU and register file. It accepts a 16-bit instruction input and produces an 8-bit result output. The design is flexible for expansion but is not a complete processor. Testing is done via a cocotb testbench with various test cases.
